anomalies.observed: The netlist places zero-ohm R4 between U2.6 (A) and J4.3, and zero-ohm R8 between J4.3 and J8.3, so the transceiver line and both servo signals are joined. It also places the two alternative bus-pin jumpers R7/R18 on the same PWM1 signal node, and R12/R23 on the same PWM2 signal node. R11 and R17 connect those PWM nodes to the servo signal pins through 1 kΩ resistors.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes mutually exclusive PWM and serial configurations: PWM should provide two independent GPIO signal paths and leave PortC unused; serial should bridge the servo signals to the shared transceiver bus. The alternative GPIO bus-pin jumpers should likewise be selected per core variant, not both connected.

evidence.quote: PWM mode: each servo header's signal pin gets its own independent 1 kΩ-buffered GPIO line ... PortC ... is left completely unused.
Serial mode ... J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 are tied together into one shared bus node and driven by U1 ... Schematic annotation: "Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo".
"Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others"

anomalies.impact: As represented, the PWM GPIO paths are not independent and are connected to the shared servo/transceiver signal network; both alternative GPIO mappings are also joined. This can cause GPIO contention or unintended loading, prevent PortC from remaining available in PWM mode, and make servo operation dependent on the selected population configuration.

parsed.summary: The netlist connects the transceiver line, both servo signals, and the PWM signal paths into a shared network, and it connects both alternatives for each GPIO jumper selection. That conflicts with the specified mutually exclusive modes and independent PWM channels.
